subject: EU data contracting & DPA/SCC next steps
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Dobson <anna.dobson@oakmonthealth.org>, oakmont-procurement@oakmonthealth.org
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2026 09:18:00 +0100
Subject: Follow-up: GDPR/DPA + SCC modules — quick recap and asks

Anna / team,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can keep legal/procurement moving: 

- Summary of call: Oakmont will act as the data controller for patient records and clinical telemetry. Redwood would be engaged to provide inference as a processor for the hosted inference service (prod).
- Immediate asks from Oakmont: DPA (your requested template), confirmation of which SCC module we intend to adopt for transfers (if any), SOC 2 report availability, and kickoff of your vendor security questionnaire.

What we can do straight away:
1) Share our DPA draft tailored for processor relationships. (I’m attaching an initial draft for your review.)
2) Recommend SCC approach for RDC-to-EU hosting vs fallback to US-based processing — will propose Module 2 (processor) + supplementary clauses for processors transferring to sub-processors in the US.
3) Provide SOC 2 Type II summary + scope and our compliance pack with encryption/kms details.
4) Start and return your vendor questionnaire — please send the spreadsheet if you want us to complete directly.

Next steps proposed:
- I’ll send the DPA draft and our compliance pack by EOD today (Alex will pick up the SOC 2 details).
- Suggest a short legal-only sync (30 min) between Oakmont legal and our GC/Product security next week to finalize DPA/SCC selection.

If that plan works, I’ll route docs to procurement and legal and we can lock a time.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: Redwood_DPA_Draft_v1.pdf (draft)
From: Anna Dobson <anna.dobson@oakmonthealth.org>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: oakmont-procurement@oakmonthealth.org
Date: Thu, 13 May 2026 10:02:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Follow-up: GDPR/DPA + SCC modules — quick recap and asks

Thanks Rishi — appreciate the quick follow-up and recap. A few clarifications from our side before legal digs in: 

- Confirming Oakmont is the controller for patient data; we expect Redwood to be the processor for any inference on PHI/pseudonymized datasets.
- HIPAA/BAA: Oakmont handles PHI; we need to understand whether Redwood will require a BAA in addition to the DPA, or if the engagement can be scoped to exclude PHI processing. Please advise.
- Data residency: Oakmont prefers EU residency for live production data. If Redwood uses US sub-processors, we will need SCCs (Module 2 or equivalent) and clarity on SCC module selection.
- Vendor security questionnaire: attaching the procurement SQ (spreadsheet). Please confirm who on your side will complete it and an estimated ETA.

Can you also share your SOC 2 Type II report or a summary of the scope (services, dates, auditor)? We’ll likely want an executive summary first.

Happy to set a legal sync once we have the DPA draft and SOC summary.

Thanks,
Anna Dobson
Procurement Lead | Oakmont Health
anna.dobson@oakmonthealth.org

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Dobson <anna.dobson@oakmonthealth.org>, oakmont-procurement@oakmonthealth.org
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 11:30:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Follow-up: GDPR/DPA + SCC modules — initial materials attached

On Thu, 13 May 2026 at 10:02 +0200 Anna Dobson wrote:
> Can you also share your SOC 2 Type II report or a summary of the scope (services, dates, auditor)?

Anna — thanks. Attaching the DPA draft (processor-focused) and a short compliance pack that contains: SOC 2 Type II summary (production inference runtime only), our list of sub-processors, data residency options, and KMS/encryption practices. A few notes inline below: 

- DPA: drafted with Oakmont as controller / Redwood as processor. We included standard processor obligations plus a sub-processor onboarding clause and an EU data residency preference field. Open to your edits.
- SCC recommendation: for processor relationships where transfers to US sub-processors are possible we typically propose Module 2 (processor) plus the modernized SCC clauses. If Oakmont requires a more restrictive approach (no transfers), we can pin the instance to EU-only regions and contractually restrict transfers.
- SOC 2: We completed SOC 2 Type II covering the inference service from 2025-06-01 to 2026-05-31; third-party audit by Clearlane LLP. Summary included in the compliance pack; full report available under NDA.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Draft_v1.pdf; Redwood_Compliance_Pack_v2.zip

Proposed ETA: we can complete the vendor questionnaire within 3 business days after you confirm the preferred scope (PHI in/out, SCC preference). If you prefer, we’ll fill the spreadsheet directly — let us know.

Regards,
Alex Martinez
Head of Solutions | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai
From: Lucas Brown <lucas.brown@oakmonthealth.org>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: oakmont-procurement@oakmonthealth.org
Date: Mon, 17 May 2026 09:05:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Follow-up: GDPR/DPA + SCC modules — initial materials attached

Alex / team,

Appreciate the materials. A couple of security/legal points before we schedule the legal sync: 

1) HIPAA / BAA: Oakmont will require a BAA if PHI is being processed. If your production service will ever touch PHI we will need Redwood to execute a BAA. If you’re able to guarantee PHI will not be processed (hard data separation / pseudonymization enforced by us) that changes our expectations; please confirm the technical controls you can enforce.
2) Key management / encryption: confirm encryption at rest and in transit, and whether Redwood allows customer-managed keys (CMKs) — we prefer CMKs for production.
3) SCC module: Oakmont legal prefers Module 2 with processor clauses; see inline suggested edits on the DPA about liability caps and audit access.

Please have your security lead respond to points 1–2 and circulate an updated DPA with the suggested SCC language ahead of the sync. Also — we will upload a completed SQ if you can fill the vendor spreadsheet directly and return.

Thanks,
Lucas Brown
CISO | Oakmont Health
lucas.brown@oakmonthealth.org
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Dobson <anna.dobson@oakmonthealth.org>, Lucas Brown <lucas.brown@oakmonthealth.org>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2026 15:20:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Follow-up: GDPR/DPA + SCC modules — compliance materials and next steps

On Mon, 17 May 2026 at 09:05 +0200 Lucas Brown wrote:
> Please have your security lead respond to points 1–2 and circulate an updated DPA with the suggested SCC language ahead of the sync.

Lucas / Anna — thanks. Quick answers and next steps from security: 

- HIPAA / BAA: Redwood supports PHI processing and will sign a BAA where the contract scope includes PHI. If Oakmont prefers to avoid PHI at the platform layer, we can support strict tenant separation and filtering at the ingestion layer but that requires joint implementation work.
- Encryption / KMS: production inference instances support encryption at rest and in transit. We offer both Redwood-managed keys and cloud CMK options (customer-managed keys via AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault). We will include the KMS configuration options in the compliance pack.
- SCC & DPA revision: we’ve applied Oakmont’s Module 2 language suggestions to the DPA draft and added audit access language. Updated DPA will be routed via DocuSign for signatures.

I’ve attached our redline and the completed vendor questionnaire (we filled the spreadsheet). Links below: 
- DocuSign DPA (preview): https://www.docusign.com/rdw/dpa/RDW-2026-0421
- Compliance pack (drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/compliance/Oakmont-Compliance-Pack
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/rdw/RDW-2026-0421

Attachments: Oakmont_Vendor_SQ_2026.xlsx (completed)

Proposed next steps:
- Legal-only sync: Wed, 19 May 2026, 14:00 CET (we can move if needed) — agenda: finalize SCC selection, confirm BAA requirement, sign DPA, and lock data residency settings.
- If agreed, we’ll send DocuSign links for DPA and planned SCC module attachments after the sync.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Director, Product Security | Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
From: Anna Dobson <anna.dobson@oakmonthealth.org>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: GDPR/DPA + SCC modules — compliance materials and next steps

Grace / team — that works for us. We’ve reviewed the updates and the completed questionnaire looks good. Confirming the legal sync: Wed, 19 May 2026 at 14:00 CET (30 min).

Action items before the sync:
- Redwood to share the DocuSign DPA preview link (received) and final SCC module language in the contract redline.
- Redwood security to confirm whether CMKs can be used for the EU production instances (we prefer CMK).
- Oakmont will confirm whether PHI will be processed by Redwood (we expect internal confirmation by EOD Monday).

Thanks — looking forward to the sync.

Anna Dobson
